stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To investigate the relevance of the Symptom Checklist 90-R Obsessive-Compulsive subscale to cognition in individuals with brain tumor.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: DESIGN
stage1_evidence_shown.context: A prospective study of patients assessed with a neuropsychological test battery.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: PATIENTS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Nineteen adults with biopsy-confirmed diagnoses of malignant brain tumors were assessed prior to aggressive chemotherapy.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Included in the assessment were the Mattis Dementia Rating Scale, California Verbal Learning Test, Trail Making Test B, Symptom Checklist 90-R, Mood Assessment Scale, Beck Anxiety Inventory, and Chronic Illness Problem Inventory.

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: The SCL 90-R Obsessive-Compulsive subscale was not related to objective measures of attention, verbal memory, or age. It was related significantly to symptoms of depression (r = .81, P<.005), anxiety (r = .66, P<.005), and subjective complaints of memory problems (r = .75, P<.005). Multivariate analyses indicated that reported symptoms of depression contributed 66% of the variance in predicting SCL 90-R Obsessive-Compulsive Scores, whereas symptoms of anxiety contributed an additional 6% (P<.0001).
